correctness.rationale: The directed overlap graph is explicitly Eulerian. Rotation pairings split edges into binary necklaces; switches at word vertices merge necklace cycles. Spanning-tree switch sets realize specified cross transitions and realize an unswitched transition iff its connection edge is not a bridge. Every necklace has descending links, and a full bridge classification follows by comparing the number of ones in primitive periods with a two-step upward/downward detour for interior equally spaced necklaces. Locally admissible candidates and the support count are then exact. Actual packaged verify.py independently passed 63 undirected-bridge parameter cases (n<=13,k<=6) and 45 directed Euler-contraction parameter cases (all n<=9, all k). These finite computations are corroboration, not the all-length proof.

evidence: Sawada–Stevens–Williams (2011) establishes existence and efficient generation for all n and upper weight bounds; its stated objectives do not include the union of achievable n+1 windows across all Euler tours.
Sawada–Williams–Wong (2013) gives general weight-range gluing constructions, not a necessity-and-sufficiency description of all permissible consecutive edge pairings.
Sawada–Williams–Wong (2016) gives greedy/necklace universal-cycle constructions and minimal representative properties, not global next-window support across all tours.

The already-known unrestricted support theorem cannot directly be restricted to bounded-weight Euler tours: its connectivity argument relies on an unrestricted Hamilton cycle after removal of one vertex.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Existence, efficient construction, and cycle enumeration are logically weaker for global support of every admissible n+1 factor. General Eulerian graph theory gives an algorithmic connectivity test but does not supply the sharp bridge classification. For k=n the previous exact theorem already covers the claim; originality is asserted for the complete interior-weight law, not for that endpoint.

originality.rationale: The precise all-interior-weight support law and its k|n four-versus-two arithmetic phase change were not covered by the inspected full primary texts or relevant published records. Explicitly existing: bounded-weight cycle existence (2011), generic gluing (2013), lexicographic constructions (2016), all cycles at k=2 (2026), and unrestricted next-window support at k=n (2026). The new theorem strengthens existing knowledge over k>=3 with k<n. Priority remains qualified by possible unindexed universal-cycle adjacency literature.
residual_risks: Earlier unindexed theorem describing the transition support of all bounded-weight de Bruijn Euler tours could subsume the result.
Generic Eulerian-graph transition feasibility is known; originality resides in the exact closed necklace-bridge classification, not that criterion.
The k=2 and unrestricted k=n cases are already directly or indirectly covered by previously published results.

value.rationale: Precisely classifying which locally legal next read windows are attainable across every maximal-coverage constrained cyclic word is a natural inverse/design question. The sharp divisibility obstruction k|n is structural and persists at arbitrary order and interior Hamming bounds. This distinguishes truly impossible transitions from merely absent transitions in one construction, enabling constrained sequence and motif design. It is not a routine one-cycle enumeration, table recomputation, or marginal constant improvement.
